pages.title: How to Ask Someone to Repeat and Confirm Details in English
pages.h1: How to ask someone to repeat names, numbers, and times in English
pages.meta_description: Learn how to ask someone to repeat a name, number, or time in English—with natural phrases, a listening exercise, and confirmation practice.
pages.lede: A practical hear–commit–verify guide for the moments when one missed letter, number, name, or time changes what you need to do next.

search.primary_query: how to ask someone to repeat
supporting_queries: how to ask someone to repeat a number in English
how to confirm a time in English
what to say when you did not catch a name
natural English phrases for checking details
search.reader_task: The reader can identify exactly what they missed, ask for that part again, and say the confirmed answer back without pretending to understand.

pages.quick_answer: When a name, number, or time is unclear, make a specific request instead of asking for the whole message again. Say what you missed, confirm a likely answer, then repeat the important detail back before acting. This lets the other person correct one small part and helps you leave with the right instruction.

quick_answer_steps.label: Missed it
quick_answer_steps.phrase: Sorry, I didn’t catch the gate number. Could you say it again?
quick_answer_steps.guidance: Name the exact part you missed.

quick_answer_steps.label: Heard a likely answer
quick_answer_steps.guidance: Offer one candidate for the speaker to confirm or correct.

quick_answer_steps.label: Need to act on it
quick_answer_steps.phrase: So that’s D14, boarding at 7:20, right?
quick_answer_steps.guidance: Repeat the important details back once.

pages.practice_intro: Listen once before typing. Enter only the gate and boarding time you heard, then commit both answers. The transcript stays hidden until you submit.

response_ladder.label: Repeat
response_ladder.phrase: Sorry, I didn’t catch the gate number. Could you say it again?
response_ladder.why: Naming the missing part gives the speaker a smaller, easier request.

response_ladder.label: Confirm
response_ladder.when: You think you heard the detail.
response_ladder.why: The speaker can answer yes or correct one precise item.

response_ladder.label: Say it back
response_ladder.when: The detail affects what you do next.
response_ladder.why: One short repeat checks the two details as a usable instruction.

decision_map.example: Sorry, could you say that again?
Sorry, I didn’t catch the gate number. Could you say it again?

decision_map.signal: Two details guide the next action

dialogue.speaker: Fellow passenger
dialogue.text: They moved us to gate C9, and boarding starts at 7:25.
dialogue.note: The letter-number code and time arrive in one turn.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.note: Confirm the uncertain detail instead of repeating the whole message.

dialogue.speaker: Fellow passenger
dialogue.note: The answer supplies both actionable details again.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.note: A compact repeat closes the loop naturally.

mistakes.repair: Name the missing item: “Sorry, what was the boarding time?”
Offer your best candidate as a question: “Did you say D14?”

mistakes.problem: Repeating several possible answers as if all were correct
mistakes.repair: Ask the speaker to choose: “Was that 6:40 or 7:40?” Then keep only the confirmed value.
Use one short apology, then make the request: “Sorry, could you repeat the time?”

transfer_prompts.heard: The name or drink size was unclear.
transfer_prompts.say: Sorry, was that Mina with a medium latte?

transfer_prompts.heard: The room and start time came too quickly.
transfer_prompts.say: Just to confirm, is it Room 214 at 3:30?

transfer_prompts.heard: A visitor’s last name and appointment time were unclear.
transfer_prompts.say: Sorry, could you spell the last name? And is the appointment at 12:15?

faq.question: Is it rude to ask someone to repeat a number or time?
faq.answer: No. A short, specific request usually sounds attentive. Name the part you missed and avoid blaming the speaker.

faq.question: Should I say “repeat” or “say that again”?
faq.answer: Both work. “Could you say that again?” is broadly natural; “Could you repeat the gate number?” is useful when you can name the exact detail.

faq.question: What if I am not sure between two numbers?
faq.answer: Offer the two candidates as a question, listen to the correction, and then say back only the confirmed number.

faq.question: How can I ask someone to spell a name?
faq.answer: Say, “Sorry, I didn’t catch your name. Could you spell it?” Then repeat the letters or name back once.

faq.question: Does replaying the practice audio count as failure?
faq.answer: No. The page records a replay as assisted practice so you can distinguish first-listen recall from successful repair. Both are useful skills.

pages.title: How to Confirm a Coffee Order and Name in English
pages.h1: How to confirm a coffee order and name in English
pages.meta_description: Learn how to confirm a drink, customer name, and order changes in English with natural phrases and a short listening exercise.
pages.lede: Catch the name, drink, and changes without making the barista repeat the whole order.

how to confirm a drink order
what to say when a barista calls your name
search.reader_task: The reader can ask for the unclear part of a coffee order and repeat the confirmed name and drink back once.

pages.quick_answer: At a coffee counter, ask for the one part you missed, then confirm the name and drink together. A short check is faster than guessing or asking for the entire order again. Use the name, drink, and any change you heard, then let the barista correct one detail before you take the cup.

quick_answer_steps.label: Missed the name
quick_answer_steps.phrase: Sorry, I didn’t catch the name. Could you say it again?
quick_answer_steps.guidance: Ask for the exact missing part.

quick_answer_steps.label: Ready to take it
quick_answer_steps.phrase: So that’s Leo, a large cappuccino, and no syrup—right?

response_ladder.label: Confirm
response_ladder.why: One yes-or-no question checks the main detail.

response_ladder.label: Say it back
response_ladder.when: You are about to take the cup.
response_ladder.phrase: So that’s Leo, a large cappuccino, and no syrup—right?
response_ladder.why: A short repeat catches a final mismatch.

mistakes.repair: Check the name first: “Was that Leo?”
Name the part: “Sorry, what was the drink?”
Offer one candidate, then wait for correction.

transfer_prompts.say: Sorry, was that Nora’s almond croissant?

faq.question: Is it okay to ask a barista to repeat a name?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask briefly and name the part you missed.

faq.question: Should I repeat the whole order?
faq.answer: Only when several details matter. Otherwise, confirm the one unclear part.

faq.question: How do I check the spelling of a name?
faq.answer: Say, “Could you spell the name for me?” and repeat the letters back once.

pages.title: How to Confirm a Changed Meeting Time in English
pages.h1: How to confirm a changed meeting time and room in English
pages.meta_description: Learn how to catch a corrected meeting time or room in English, confirm the final detail, and avoid acting on the old information.
pages.lede: When someone says “not” or corrects a time, confirm the new plan—not the first number you heard.

search.primary_query: how to confirm a changed meeting time
supporting_queries: how to confirm a meeting room in English
what to say when someone corrects a time
how to ask about a schedule change in English
search.reader_task: The reader can identify the corrected room or time and repeat the final plan back before the meeting starts.

pages.quick_answer: When a meeting detail changes, listen for the correction and confirm the final value. Do not repeat the first time or room just because it arrived first. Ask which detail is current, then say the room and time back together so you can act on one clear plan.

quick_answer_steps.label: Heard two values
quick_answer_steps.guidance: Ask the speaker to choose the current value.

quick_answer_steps.label: Heard a correction
quick_answer_steps.phrase: So the meeting is at 2:45, not 3:00?

pages.practice_intro: Listen once. Enter the room and final meeting time before the transcript appears.

response_ladder.label: Separate
response_ladder.why: A choice question makes the correction clear.

response_ladder.label: Confirm
response_ladder.phrase: So the meeting is at 2:45, not 3:00?
response_ladder.why: It checks which value replaced the other.

response_ladder.label: Say it back
response_ladder.why: One compact plan is easy to use.

dialogue.speaker: Classmate
dialogue.text: The workshop is in Room 108 at 2:45, not 3:00.
dialogue.note: The correction comes at the end.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.note: Confirm the final plan.

dialogue.speaker: Classmate
dialogue.note: The reply separates old and current information.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.note: The confirmation is complete.

mistakes.problem: Keeping the first number you hear

mistakes.repair: When both matter, say the room and time together.

mistakes.problem: Asking for the full message again
mistakes.repair: Ask which time or room is current.

transfer_prompts.say: Just to confirm, Friday instead of Thursday?
So the table is for 7:00, not 7:30?
Could you send the new link once more?

faq.question: How do I check which time is correct?
faq.answer: Ask, “Which time is correct?” or offer the two values as a choice.

faq.question: Is “not 3:00?” polite?
faq.answer: Yes, when your tone is neutral and you are checking a clear correction.

faq.question: Should I repeat the room too?
faq.answer: Yes, if going to the wrong room would cause a problem.

pages.title: How to Ask for and Confirm Bus Directions in English
pages.h1: How to ask for and confirm bus directions in English
pages.meta_description: Learn how to ask for and confirm bus directions in English, including the stop, street, route number, and direction of travel.
pages.lede: Turn a fast set of directions into one clear route before you get off the bus.

search.primary_query: how to ask for and confirm bus directions
supporting_queries: how to ask which bus to take in English
how to confirm a bus stop in English
search.reader_task: The reader can ask for one unclear direction and repeat the stop, route, and destination back in the right order.

pages.quick_answer: For bus directions, ask about the missing step, then repeat the route in order. Confirm the stop, street, bus number, and destination only when each one matters. A short route summary helps the driver correct one turn before you get off, instead of leaving you to guess after the bus has moved on.

quick_answer_steps.phrase: Sorry, which street do I cross?
quick_answer_steps.guidance: Ask for the exact part you missed.

quick_answer_steps.label: Heard the route
quick_answer_steps.phrase: Do I take the 14 toward Central Station?
quick_answer_steps.guidance: Confirm the route and direction together.

quick_answer_steps.label: Ready to move
quick_answer_steps.phrase: Get off at the museum, cross King Street, then take the 14—right?

response_ladder.why: Route number and direction belong together.

response_ladder.why: The order matters as much as the words.

pages.title: How to Confirm a Wait Time and Phone Number in English
pages.h1: How to confirm a wait time and phone number in English
pages.meta_description: Learn how to confirm a restaurant wait time and phone-number ending in English with short, natural phrases and listening practice.
pages.lede: Catch the time and digits once, then repeat them back before the host sends a text.

search.primary_query: how to confirm a wait time and phone number
supporting_queries: how to confirm a phone number in English
how to ask about a restaurant wait in English
how to repeat phone digits in English
search.reader_task: The reader can confirm a wait estimate and phone-number ending without confusing or losing a digit.

pages.quick_answer: When a host gives a wait and phone-number ending, check the time first and repeat the digits slowly. Ask for one number again if you are unsure; do not guess. A brief readout lets the host correct a single digit before they send the text, which is easier than fixing a missed message later.

quick_answer_steps.label: Missed the wait
quick_answer_steps.phrase: Sorry, how long is the wait?

quick_answer_steps.label: Need the text
quick_answer_steps.phrase: About 20 minutes, and the number ends 4-8-1-7—right?

response_ladder.why: Ask for the one number you missed.

response_ladder.label: Confirm
response_ladder.why: Separate digits are easy to check.

response_ladder.label: Say it back
response_ladder.when: The host is about to text you.
response_ladder.phrase: About 20 minutes, and the number ends 4-8-1-7—right?
response_ladder.why: A final repeat protects both details.

mistakes.repair: Say each digit separately when you confirm it.

faq.question: How should I say phone digits?
faq.answer: Say one digit at a time when accuracy matters.

faq.question: Can I ask for only the last four digits?
faq.answer: Yes. “Could I confirm the last four digits?” is natural and specific.

faq.question: What if the wait is only an estimate?
faq.answer: Say “about” when you repeat it: “About 20 minutes, right?”
